headline: BPP on the RoboTwin Same Scene benchmark
not_a_competition_score: This is not a score in either field. The policy was shown the demonstration's frames, action trajectory and proprioception, and was scored from the identical scene it was shown. The video-only field withholds the actions and proprioception; the sensorimotor field scores from a different initial state. No field allows this combination, and under Same Scene the demonstrated actions are close to the answer - the benchmark's own replay oracle succeeds on this scene by feeding them straight back.

protocol.demonstration_source: RoboTwin's own scripted expert, generated at evaluation time
protocol.scored_from: the identical initial scene as the demonstration

demonstration_shown.note: The adapter converts the demonstration to end-effector poses and gripper commands and feeds them to the policy alongside the frames. That is more than the video-only field shows, which is why this number cannot be read as a video-only result.

subject.label: BPP (behavior prompting)
subject.why_not_admissible: It is the sensorimotor field's current genesis policy, and its architecture takes the demonstration's actions as input - which the video-only field has no channel for.

ceiling.label: What the harness itself achieves on this scene
ceiling.why: The benchmark's replay oracle feeds the demonstration's own actions straight back into the identical scene. It is not an entrant and not a policy: it is the measurement that says the episode is winnable and the scene reconstructs exactly, so a zero above means the model failed rather than that the task was impossible. It is also why handing a policy those actions under Same Scene measures copying - which is the whole reason the video-only field withholds them. Same task and same scene seed as the row above; the oracle ran under the stock camera profile, so the two runs are not a single table and the benchmark says so itself, below.
